The paper's stated scope is an arbitrary connected linear Lie group, where generators need not be diagonalizable (e.g. nilpotent $\varrho=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $N=2$, trivial $L$: $\ker M_d$ is 2-dimensional but only one eigenvector product exists). issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:added-1 ($\mathrm{diff}_g\rho=\rho(g)\,\mathrm{diff}_e\rho$) is a property of group homomorphisms; its proof uses $\rho(h)=\rho(g)\rho(hg^{-1})$ (which is itself wrong as written, since $\rho(g)\rho(hg^{-1})=\rho(ghg^{-1})$). Corollary cor:constant_zero applies it to a scalar function $\rho=\sum c_{\bbm,\bbm'}\rho^{\bl}_{\bbm,\bbm'}$, which is not a representation, so the inference fails and the conclusion is false: e.g. for $SO(3)$, $\rho=D^1_{00}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=\cos\beta$ has all Euler-angle derivatives at the identity equal to zero by eq:deri_alpha–eq:deri_gamma, yet is not constant. The reverse implication in prop:GE_basis and thm:GEPI_basis ($\bc\in\ker M \Rightarrow$ GE) rests entirely on this corollary. The true statement needed is that for connected $G$, a matrix $C$ intertwining the Lie algebra actions ($d\rho^{\bl}(X)^TC=C\,d\rho^L(X)^T$ for all $X$) intertwines the group actions; this requires a different argument (e.g. $t\mapsto\rho^{\bl}(e^{tX})^T C\rho^L(e^{-tX})^T$ has zero derivative, then use that $\exp(\mathfrak g)$ generates $G$).
